metaDescription: Paayap (BPI Cp 1) cowpea is a cowpea variety. About 63 days to harvest, 1.3 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Paayap (BPI Cp 1) is a registered cowpea variety, also sold or known as Paayap or BPI Cp 1. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1976. It takes about 63 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 1.26 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Paayap (BPI Cp 1) cowpea
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Paayap (BPI Cp 1) cowpea takes about 63 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 9.7 days longer than the average of the 13 cowpea varieties with a day count, 53.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.26 t/ha trails the average of its group, 5.44. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 63 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit cowpea fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
The seed coat is mottle purple.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Very dark green pods, mottled purple seeds.
Resistant to fusarium wilt and rust.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: bPI Cp 1, on the Philippine Seed Board list since 1976 and named with the Filipino word for cowpea, current seed sellers not confirmed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Paayap (BPI Cp 1) cowpea

Cowpea fits the dry season after rice, on the moisture the paddy keeps. Pick by use: green pods for vegetables, or dry seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: Is Paayap the same as Paayap (BPI Cp 1)?
items.a: Yes. Paayap is another name for Paayap (BPI Cp 1). Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 63 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.26 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Paayap (BPI Cp 1)?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
